blocks.en: Designing Resource Sharing
blocks.zh_html: 资源共享设计(Designing Resource Sharing)

blocks.en: Sharing Resources: Statistical Multiplexing
blocks.zh_html: 资源共享：统计复用(Statistical Multiplexing)

blocks.en: Links and switches on the Internet have finite capacity. One key design problem we need to solve is: How do we share these resources between different Internet users?
blocks.zh_html: 互联网(Internet)上的链路(links)和交换机(switches)容量(capacity)有限。我们需要解决的一个关键设计问题是：如何在不同的互联网用户之间共享这些资源？

blocks.en: Let’s formalize the problem a bit more. Recall that a flow is a stream of packets exchanged between two end hosts (e.g. a video call between you and a friend). The Internet needs to support many simultaneous flows at the same time, despite limited capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 让我们把问题再形式化一点。回忆一下，流(flow)是在两个终端主机(end hosts)之间交换的分组流，例如你和朋友之间的视频通话。互联网(Internet)需要在容量(capacity)有限的情况下同时支持许多并发的流(flows)。

blocks.en: We often say that the network resources are statistically multiplexed, which means that we’ll dynamically allocate resources to users based on their demand, instead of partitioning a fixed share of resources to users.
blocks.zh_html: 我们常说网络资源是统计复用(statistically multiplexed)的，这意味着我们会根据用户的需求动态地分配资源，而不是将固定的资源份额预先划分给用户。

blocks.en: As an analogy, consider your personal computer. It’s not the case that your computer preemptively allocates half its CPU to Firefox, and half its CPU to Zoom, and only allows each application to use its half of the CPU. Instead, your computer dynamically allocates resources to different applications depending on their needs.
blocks.zh_html: 打个比方，想象你的个人电脑。你的电脑不会预先将一半的 CPU 分配给 Firefox，另一半分配给 Zoom，且只允许每个应用使用分配给它的那一半。相反，你的计算机会根据不同应用的需求，动态地分配资源。

blocks.en: Statistical multiplexing is now everywhere in computer science. For example, in cloud computing, different companies might dynamically share resources in a datacenter.
blocks.zh_html: 统计复用(statistical multiplexing)如今在计算机科学中无处不在。例如，在云计算(cloud computing)中，不同公司可能会动态地共享数据中心(datacenter)中的资源。

blocks.en: Statistical multiplexing is a great way to efficiently share network resources, because user demand changes over time. You probably aren’t using a constant 10 Mbps of bandwidth every second, 24 hours a day. You probably have more demand while you’re awake, and less while you’re sleeping.
blocks.zh_html: 统计复用(statistical multiplexing)是高效共享网络资源的好方法，因为用户的需求随时间变化。你可能不会 24 小时每秒都使用恒定的 10 Mbps 带宽(bandwidth)。你在清醒时需求可能更高，而睡眠时需求更低。

blocks.en: The premise that makes statistical multiplexing work is: In practice, the peak of aggregate demand is much less than the aggregate of peak demands.
blocks.zh_html: 使统计复用(statistical multiplexing)有效的前提是：在实践中，总需求的峰值(peak of aggregate demand)远小于各峰值需求之和(aggregate of peak demands)。

blocks.en: Let’s unpack what this means. Suppose we have two users, A and B. We can plot each user’s demand over time.
blocks.zh_html: 让我们解释一下这意味着什么。假设有两个用户 A 和 B。我们可以绘制每个用户随时间变化的需求曲线。

blocks.en: How much capacity do we need to allocate in order to fully meet both users’ demands?
blocks.zh_html: 我们需要分配多少容量(capacity)才能完全满足两个用户的需求？

blocks.en: The bad strategy (no statistical multiplexing) is to compute the aggregate of peak demands. We find A’s peak demand and B’s peak demand, and add them together.
blocks.zh_html: 糟糕的策略（无统计复用(statistical multiplexing)）是计算各峰值需求之和(aggregate of peak demands)。我们找到 A 的峰值需求和 B 的峰值需求，然后将它们相加。

blocks.en: If we allocate this much capacity, we can definitely meet their demands. A’s peak demand is X, so we allocate X to A, and likewise, we allocate Y to B. However, this approach is wasteful, because A’s peak and B’s peak didn’t happen at the same time.
blocks.zh_html: 如果分配这么多容量(capacity)，我们肯定能满足他们的需求。A 的峰值需求是 X，所以我们给 A 分配 X；同样，给 B 分配 Y。但这种方法是浪费的，因为 A 的峰值和 B 的峰值并没有在同一时间发生。

blocks.en: The better strategy (statistical multiplexing) is to first compute the aggregate demand by graphing their combined demand over time. For example, the 10am demand in the new graph is the A’s 10am demand, plus B’s 10am demand. Then, we compute the peak of the aggregate demand.
blocks.zh_html: 更好的策略（统计复用(statistical multiplexing)）是首先绘制合并需求随时间变化的总需求曲线。例如，新图中上午 10 点的需求是 A 在上午 10 点的需求加上 B 在上午 10 点的需求。然后，我们计算总需求的峰值(peak of the aggregate demand)。

blocks.en: If we allocate this much capacity, we can no longer statically allocate a portion to each user. However, by dynamically changing the amount we allocate to each user over time, we can still successfully meet their demands, even while having less capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 如果分配这么多容量(capacity)，我们就不能再静态地为每个用户分配固定份额。然而，通过随时间动态调整分配给每个用户的资源量，即使使用更少的容量，我们仍然可以满足他们的需求。

blocks.en: The statistical multiplexing approach allows us to support the same users with less capacity (cheaper for us, more efficient use of resources). For many distributions, we can show that the peak of the aggregate is actually closer to the sum of the average demands, which is much less than the sum of the peak demands.
blocks.zh_html: 统计复用(statistical multiplexing)方法让我们用更少的容量(capacity)支持同样的用户（更便宜、更高效地使用资源）。对于许多分布，可以证明总需求的峰值实际上更接近平均需求之和(sum of average demands)，这远小于峰值需求之和(sum of peak demands)。

blocks.en: In practice, in the network, we don’t provision for the absolute worst case, when everything peaks at the same time. Instead, we share resources dynamically and hope that peaks don’t occur at the same time. Peaks could still happen at the same time, which would cause packets to be delayed or dropped (recall the link queue). Nevertheless, we made the design choice to statistically multiplex and use resources more efficiently, while dealing with the consequences (occasional simultaneous peaks).
blocks.zh_html: 在实践中，在网络中，我们不会按绝对最坏情况（所有峰值同时出现）来规划容量(capacity)。相反，我们动态共享资源，并希望峰值不会同时发生。峰值仍然可能同时出现，这会导致分组(packets)被延迟或丢弃（回想一下链路队列(link queue)）。尽管如此，我们仍然选择统计复用(statistical multiplexing)以更高效地利用资源，同时承担偶尔出现并发峰值的后果。

blocks.en: At the end of the day, statistical multiplexing is a design choice with trade-offs, and different users might make different choices. For example, financial exchanges sometimes decide to build their own dedicated networks to support peak demand, because they care more about ensuring network connectivity during peak periods, and they can afford the extra cost.
blocks.zh_html: 归根结底，统计复用(statistical multiplexing)是一个充满权衡(trade-offs)的设计选择，不同的用户可能会做出不同的决定。例如，金融交易所有时会决定构建自己的专用网络(dedicated networks)以支持峰值需求，因为他们更关心峰值期间的网络连通性，并且能够承担额外成本。

blocks.en: Sharing Resources: Circuit Switching vs. Packet Switching
blocks.zh_html: 资源共享：电路交换 vs. 分组交换(Circuit Switching vs. Packet Switching)

blocks.en: We now know that we can use statistical multiplexing to decide how much capacity to build. Our next question is: How do we actually dynamically allocate resources between users?
blocks.zh_html: 我们现在知道可以用统计复用(statistical multiplexing)来决定建造多少容量(capacity)。接下来的问题是：我们实际上如何动态地在用户之间分配资源？

blocks.en: As an analogy, consider a popular restaurant with many customers and a limited supply of tables. There are two ways we could imagine allocating tables to customers. We could have customers make reservations, or we could seat customers first-come first-serve.
blocks.zh_html: 打个比方，想象一家热门餐厅，顾客很多而餐位有限。有两种分配餐位的方式：让顾客预约(reservations)，或者先到先服务(first-come first-serve)。

blocks.en: The two approaches to sharing resources in the network are similar. One approach is best-effort. Everybody sends their data into the network, without making any reservations, and hopes for the best. There’s no guarantee that there will be enough bandwidth to meet your demand.
blocks.zh_html: 网络中资源共享的两种方式与此类似。一种方式是尽力而为(best-effort)。每个人都将数据发送到网络中，不做任何预约(reservations)，然后期待最好的结果。不能保证有足够的带宽(bandwidth)来满足你的需求。

blocks.en: The canonical design for best-effort is called packet switching. The switch looks at each packet independently and forwards the packet closer to its destination. The switches don’t think about flows or reservations.
blocks.zh_html: 尽力而为(best-effort)的经典设计称为分组交换(packet switching)。交换机(switch)独立地查看每个分组(packet)，将其转发到更接近目的地的方向。交换机不关心流(flows)或预约(reservations)。

blocks.en: In addition to packets being independent from each other, the switches are also independent from each other. As a packet hops across switches, every switch considers the packet independently (the switches don’t coordinate).
blocks.zh_html: 除了分组(packets)之间相互独立，交换机(switches)之间也是相互独立的。当分组在交换机之间跳转(hop)时，每个交换机都独立地处理该分组（交换机之间不协调(coordinate)）。

blocks.en: The other approach is based on reservations. At the start of a flow, users explicitly request and reserve the bandwidth they need. After the data is sent, the resources can be released for others to reserve.
blocks.zh_html: 另一种方式基于预约(reservations)。在流(flow)开始时，用户显式地请求并预约(reserve)他们需要的带宽(bandwidth)。数据发送完毕后，资源可以被释放供他人预约。

blocks.en: The canonical design for reservations, explored in both research and industry, is called circuit switching.
blocks.zh_html: 在研究和工业界都探索过的预约(reservations)经典设计称为电路交换(circuit switching)。

blocks.en: At the start of a flow, the end hosts identify a path (sequence of switches and links) through the network, using some routing algorithm. (We haven’t discussed routing algorithms to find this path yet, so you can assume it happens by magic for now.)
blocks.zh_html: 在流(flow)开始时，终端主机(end hosts)使用某种路由算法(routing algorithm)在网络中确定一条路径(path)，即交换机(switches)和链路(links)的序列。（我们还没有讨论寻找路径的路由算法，所以暂时可以假设这是通过魔法实现的。）

blocks.en: Then, the source sends a special reservation request message to the destination. Along the way, every switch hears about this request as well. If every switch accepts the request, then the reservation is made, and a circuit of switches has been established between the source and destination.
blocks.zh_html: 然后，源端(source)向目的地发送一条特殊的预约请求(reservation request)消息。沿途的每个交换机(switch)都会收到这个请求。如果每个交换机都接受该请求，则预约成功，源端和目的地之间就建立了一条由交换机组成的电路(circuit)。

blocks.en: Once the reservation is confirmed by every switch, data can be sent. Eventually, when the flow ends, the source sends a teardown message to the recipient. Along the way, every switch sees this message and releases its capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 一旦所有交换机(switch)确认预约，数据就可以开始发送。最终，当流(flow)结束时，源端(source)向接收方发送一条拆除(teardown)消息。沿途每个交换机都会看到这条消息并释放其容量(capacity)。

blocks.en: Note: We use the term circuit here because this idea came from the phone network, which uses this same idea to allow two people to call each other.
blocks.zh_html: 注意：我们在这里使用术语电路(circuit)，是因为这个想法来自电话网络(phone network)，它使用相同的思路让两个人互相通话。

blocks.en: Remember, both circuit switching and packet switching are embodying statistical multiplexing. The main difference is the granularity at which we’re allocating resources: per-flow with reservations, or per-packet with best-effort. Even in circuit switching, we’re dynamically allocating resources based on reservations. We are not preemptively reserving for all flows that might ever exist.
blocks.zh_html: 请记住，电路交换(circuit switching)和分组交换(packet switching)都体现了统计复用(statistical multiplexing)。主要区别在于资源分配的粒度：是基于预约(reservations)的按流(per-flow)分配，还是基于尽力而为(best-effort)的按分组(per-packet)分配。即使在电路交换中，我们也是基于预约动态分配资源，而不是为所有可能存在的流预先保留资源。

blocks.en: Circuit Switching vs. Packet Switching Trade-offs
blocks.zh_html: 电路交换 vs. 分组交换的权衡(Circuit Switching vs. Packet Switching Trade-offs)

blocks.en: We now have two approaches to sharing resources on the Internet. Which is better? It depends on the criteria we’re using to evaluate each approach.
blocks.zh_html: 我们现在有两种在互联网(Internet)上共享资源的方式。哪种更好？这取决于我们用来评估每种方式的标准(criteria)。

blocks.en: There are four dimensions we can use to compare the two approaches.
blocks.zh_html: 我们可以从四个维度(dimensions)来比较这两种方式。

blocks.en: Is this a good abstraction (or API) for the network to offer to an application developer?
blocks.zh_html: 这是网络向应用开发者提供的好的抽象(abstraction)或 API 吗？

blocks.en: Circuit switching offers a more useful abstraction to developers, because there’s a guarantee of reserved bandwidth. This gives the developer more predictable and understandable behavior (assuming all goes well). As an analogy, consider reserving a machine in the cloud to run some task. It’s easier for the developer to reason about performance if they know the specs of the machine they’re getting. If the developer had no idea what machine they were using, the task could still run, but the performance is less predictable.
blocks.zh_html: 电路交换(circuit switching)为开发者提供了更有用的抽象，因为它保证了预约的带宽(bandwidth)。这给了开发者更可预测(predictable)和更易理解的行为（假设一切顺利）。打个比方，想象在云中预约一台机器来运行某个任务。如果开发者知道他们得到的机器规格(specs)，就更容易推理其性能(performance)。如果开发者完全不知道他们在用什么机器，任务可能仍然可以运行，但性能就较难预测了。

blocks.en: Circuit switching is also a useful abstraction if you’re a network operator who has to distribute resources to users. You know exactly how much bandwidth each user is requesting, and you can charge them the appropriate amount of money. It’s a little harder to implement an intuitive business model if there are no guarantees about what you’re offering to a client.
blocks.zh_html: 如果你是需要向用户分配资源的网络运营者(network operator)，电路交换(circuit switching)也是一个有用的抽象。你确切地知道每个用户请求了多少带宽(bandwidth)，并可以向他们收取相应费用。如果对你向客户提供的东西没有任何保证，实现一个直观的商业模式(business model)就会困难一些。

blocks.en: Is the approach efficient at scale? Does the approach use all the available bandwidth on the network, or is some bandwidth wasted?
blocks.zh_html: 这种方案在大规模下是否高效？它能充分利用网络中所有可用的带宽(bandwidth)，还是会浪费一些带宽？

blocks.en: Packet switching is typically more efficient. Exactly how much better depends on the burstiness of the traffic sources.
blocks.zh_html: 分组交换(packet switching)通常更高效。具体好多少取决于流量源(traffic sources)的突发性(burstiness)。

blocks.en: If each sender sends data at a constant rate throughout time, then both circuit switching and packet switching makes full use of the capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 如果每个发送方都以恒定速率(constant rate)发送数据，那么电路交换(circuit switching)和分组交换(packet switching)都能充分利用容量(capacity)。

blocks.en: By contrast, if each sender’s rate varies over time, then packet switching gives us a better use of bandwidth.
blocks.zh_html: 相比之下，如果每个发送方的速率随时间变化，那么分组交换(packet switching)能更好地利用带宽(bandwidth)。

blocks.en: Here’s an example of demand varying over time. With reservations, the three flows must reserve 12, 11, and 13 Mbps. One of the reservations will be rejected, since we can only distribute 30 Mbps.
blocks.zh_html: 这是一个需求随时间变化的例子。使用预约(reservations)，三个流(flows)必须预约 12、11 和 13 Mbps。其中一个预约将被拒绝，因为我们只能分配 30 Mbps。

blocks.en: This approach is wasting bandwidth in two different ways. The flow reserving 12 Mbps is not actually using its bandwidth for most of its time. Also, if the 12 Mbps and 11 Mbps flows get reservations, we have 7 Mbps left over that isn’t being reserved by anybody.
blocks.zh_html: 这种方法在两个方面浪费了带宽(bandwidth)。预约 12 Mbps 的流(flow)在大部分时间里实际上并没有使用其带宽。此外，如果 12 Mbps 和 11 Mbps 的流获得了预约，我们还有 7 Mbps 没有被任何人预约。

blocks.en: By contrast, in the packet switching approach, where we just send packets as they arrive, the total amount of bandwidth being used at any time never exceeds 30 Mbps. We can support every flow with the bandwidth we have.
blocks.zh_html: 相比之下，在分组交换(packet switching)方案中，我们只是按到达顺序发送分组(packets)，任何时候使用的总带宽(bandwidth)都不会超过 30 Mbps。我们可以用现有的带宽支持所有流(flows)。

blocks.en: Formally, the burstiness of a flow is defined by the ratio between its peak rate and its average rate. There’s no clear threshold for when something is smooth or bursty (they’re more descriptive terms).
blocks.zh_html: 形式化地说，流(flow)的突发性(burstiness)由其峰值速率(peak rate)与平均速率(average rate)之比定义。对于何时算平滑(smooth)或突发(bursty)，没有明确的阈值——它们更多是描述性术语。

blocks.en: Voice calls usually have smoother ratios like 3:1, while web browsing usually has burstier ratios like 100:1. (Voice calls having a smooth ratio is also why the phone network used reservations!)
blocks.zh_html: 语音通话(voice calls)通常有较平滑的比率，例如 3:1；而网页浏览(web browsing)通常有更突发的比率，例如 100:1。（语音通话的平滑比率也正是电话网络使用预约(reservations)的原因！）

blocks.en: Another reason why packet switching is more efficient is: Circuit switching spends additional time setting up and tearing down a circuit. This is especially inefficient for very short flows (e.g. downloading a tiny file).
blocks.zh_html: 分组交换(packet switching)更高效的另一个原因是：电路交换(circuit switching)在建立(setting up)和拆除(tearing down)电路时需要额外时间。这对于非常短的流(flows)，例如下载一个小文件，尤其低效。

blocks.en: How well does each approach handle failure at scale?
blocks.zh_html: 每种方法在大规模下处理故障(failure)的能力如何？

blocks.en: Packet switching is better at handling failure at scale. If a router fails, we can just send packets along a different path in the network. (We haven’t discussed how yet, but it turns out routing algorithms are good at adjusting to failure.) The end host doesn’t have to do anything different.
blocks.zh_html: 分组交换(packet switching)在大规模故障处理方面更好。如果一个路由器(router)发生故障，我们可以直接将分组(packets)沿网络中的另一条路径发送。（我们还没有讨论具体如何实现，但事实证明路由算法(routing algorithms)非常擅长适应故障。）终端主机(end host)不需要做任何额外的操作。

blocks.en: By contrast, in circuit switching, if a router along the path fails, the network still has to find a new path, but there’s more for the end host to do. The host has to somehow detect failure, and it has to resend a reservation request. It also has to free up the reservation along the old path somehow. What if the new reservation request is rejected?
blocks.zh_html: 相比之下，在电路交换(circuit switching)中，如果路径上的一个路由器(router)发生故障，网络仍然需要找到新的路径，但终端主机(end host)要做的事情就多得多。主机必须以某种方式检测故障，并重新发送预约请求(reservation request)。它还必须以某种方式释放旧路径上的预约。如果新的预约请求被拒绝怎么办？

blocks.en: This failure mode scales poorly. If a single router goes down, but millions of flows were using that router, then millions of reservation requests have to be simultaneously re-established.
blocks.zh_html: 这种故障模式(failure mode)的扩展性很差。如果单个路由器(router)宕机，而有数百万个流(flows)正在使用该路由器，那么数百万个预约请求必须同时重新建立。

blocks.en: We won’t solve these problems in detail, but hopefully you’re getting a sense that handling failures in circuit switching is a pretty hard problem.
blocks.zh_html: 我们不会详细解决这些问题，但希望你已经开始感受到：在电路交换(circuit switching)中处理故障是一个相当困难的问题。

blocks.en: How complex is it to implement each approach at scale?
blocks.zh_html: 每种方法在大规模下实现的复杂度如何？

blocks.en: If you actually tried to design circuit switching, a lot of additional design questions start to make the protocol really complicated, really quickly.
blocks.zh_html: 如果你真的尝试设计电路交换(circuit switching)，大量额外的设计问题会很快使协议(protocol)变得非常复杂。

blocks.en: How do the routers know that the reservation was successful? When 2 sees the request and agrees, how does it know that 3 and 4 also agreed? (Possible approach: We send a confirmation back in the other direction, indicating that the reservation is confirmed.)
blocks.zh_html: 路由器(routers)如何知道预约(reservation)成功了？当 2 看到请求并同意后，它如何知道 3 和 4 也同意了？（可能的方案：我们沿另一方向发回一条确认(confirmation)，表示预约已确认。）

blocks.en: What if the reservation request is lost along the way? 1 and 2 agree, but the request packet is dropped before it reaches 3 and 4. (Possible approach: Set a timer, and if the reservation isn’t confirmed in time, delete the reservation. Now the end host has to try again.)
blocks.zh_html: 如果预约请求(reservation request)在传输途中丢失了怎么办？1 和 2 同意了，但请求分组(packet)在到达 3 和 4 之前被丢弃了。（可能的方案：设置一个计时器(timer)，如果预约没有及时得到确认，就删除该预约。然后终端主机(end host)必须重试。）

blocks.en: What if the request is sent and everybody agrees, but the confirmation on the way back is dropped? 4 and 3 see the confirmation, but the confirmation packet is dropped before it reaches 2 and 1.
blocks.zh_html: 如果请求发送后所有人同意，但返回途中的确认(confirmation)被丢弃了怎么办？4 和 3 看到了确认，但确认分组(packet)在到达 2 和 1 之前被丢弃了。

blocks.en: What if the reservation is declined? Should the end host try again and request less? Should the end host wait a bit and try again with the same request? Should the router say in the rejection, “I can’t do 10 Mbps, but I can give you 8 Mbps?”
blocks.zh_html: 如果预约(reservation)被拒绝怎么办？终端主机(end host)应该重新尝试并请求更少的资源吗？还是应该稍等片刻，用同样的请求再试一次？路由器(router)应该在拒绝消息中说“我无法提供 10 Mbps，但我可以给你 8 Mbps”吗？

blocks.en: We won’t solve every design problem, but hopefully you’re noticing that circuit switching is harder to implement than it first seemed.
blocks.zh_html: 我们不会解决所有设计问题，但希望你注意到电路交换(circuit switching)实现起来比最初看起来要困难得多。

blocks.en: The fundamental problem that makes circuit switching complicated is state consensus. All the routers have to keep track of extra state, and they all have to agree on what that state is.
blocks.zh_html: 使电路交换(circuit switching)复杂的根本问题是状态共识(state consensus)。所有路由器(routers)都必须跟踪额外的状态(state)，并且它们必须就该状态是什么达成一致。

blocks.en: You might have heard of the Paxos protocols, which are extremely complicated protocols for getting multiple processors to agree on state. In practice, people to run these algorithms on a group of 4-5 servers. With circuit switching, we’re basically asking the Internet to run that on Internet scale, with millions of routers and flows.
blocks.zh_html: 你可能听说过 Paxos 协议(protocols)，这是一套极其复杂的协议，用于让多个处理器在状态(state)上达成一致。在实践中，人们通常在一组 4-5 台服务器上运行这些算法。而电路交换(circuit switching)本质上是在要求互联网(Internet)在互联网规模上运行这样的系统——面对数百万路由器(routers)和流(flows)。

blocks.en: In summary: Circuit switching gives the application better performance with reserved bandwidth. It also gives the developer more predictable behavior.
blocks.zh_html: 总结来说：电路交换(circuit switching)通过预留带宽(bandwidth)为应用(application)提供了更好的性能，也为开发者提供了更可预测(predictable)的行为。

blocks.en: However, packet switching gives us more efficient sharing of bandwidth, and avoids startup time. It also gives us easier recovery from failure, and is generally simpler to implement (less for routers to think about).
blocks.zh_html: 然而，分组交换(packet switching)让我们更高效地共享带宽(bandwidth)，避免了启动时间(startup time)，更容易从故障(failure)中恢复，并且通常实现更简单（路由器(routers)需要考虑的事情更少）。

blocks.en: Circuit Switching vs. Packet Switching In Practice
blocks.zh_html: 电路交换 vs. 分组交换：实际应用

blocks.en: In the modern Internet, packet switching is the default approach.
blocks.zh_html: 在现代互联网(Internet)中，分组交换(packet switching)是默认方案。

blocks.en: There are limited cases where circuit switching is used. For example, RSVP (Resource Reservation Protocol) can be used within a small local network, to allow routers (not end hosts) to reserve bandwidth between themselves.
blocks.zh_html: 在有限的场景中仍然使用电路交换(circuit switching)。例如，RSVP(Resource Reservation Protocol, 资源预约协议)可以在小型本地网络中使用，允许路由器(routers, 而非终端主机)之间预约带宽(bandwidth)。

blocks.en: Another use of circuit switching in the modern Internet is dedicated circuits (e.g. MPLS circuits, leased lines). As a company, you can specifically buy some Internet bandwidth (possibly including physical infrastructure) dedicated to your business. This is very expensive compared to a standard Internet connection.
blocks.zh_html: 电路交换(circuit switching)在现代互联网(Internet)中的另一个用途是专用电路(dedicated circuits)，例如 MPLS 电路、租用线路(leased lines)。作为一家公司，你可以专门购买一些互联网带宽(bandwidth)（可能包括物理基础设施），专用于你的业务。这比标准互联网连接昂贵得多。

blocks.en: Dedicated circuits are deployed at less ambitious scales than hypothetical full-Internet circuit switching. Someone usually manually sets up the reservation. The reservation is long-lived (e.g. years). The reservation is at the granularity of companies, not individual flows.
blocks.zh_html: 专用电路(dedicated circuits)在规模上比假想的全互联网电路交换小得多。通常由人工手动设置预约(reservation)。预约是长期有效的（例如按年计）。预约的粒度是公司级别，而不是单个流(flow)级别。

blocks.en: Brief history: When the Internet was first designed in the 1970s-1980s as a smaller-scale, government-funded research project, it was packet switched.
blocks.zh_html: 简要历史：互联网(Internet)最初在 1970-1980 年代作为一个小规模、政府资助的研究项目被设计出来时，就是分组交换(packet switched)的。

blocks.en: In the 1990s, when the government stopped funding the Internet and control passed over to commercial enterprises, research and industry thought we would need to change to circuit switching. The designers predicted that voice and live TV would be the main heavy-duty uses of the Internet. Both of these applications have smooth bandwidth demand, well-suited for circuit switching. Also, because ISPs had to make money off the new commercialized Internet, they thought that circuit switching would offer a more intuitive business model.
blocks.zh_html: 在 1990 年代，当政府停止资助互联网(Internet)并将控制权移交给商业企业时，研究界和工业界认为我们需要转向电路交换(circuit switching)。设计者预测语音通话和电视直播将是互联网的主要重度用途。这两种应用都有平滑的带宽(bandwidth)需求，非常适合电路交换。同时，由于 ISP 需要从新的商业化互联网中盈利，他们认为电路交换将提供更直观的商业模式(business model)。

blocks.en: There was a lot of work in research and standards bodies to implement circuit switching, but ultimately, this was a failed vision, for many of the reasons we discussed. Also, the main applications driving Internet growth were email and the web, not voice calls and TV, which is another reason why circuit switching vision didn’t work out.
blocks.zh_html: 研究机构和标准组织做了大量工作来实现电路交换(circuit switching)，但最终，这是一个失败的愿景——原因有很多，我们已讨论过其中许多。此外，推动互联网(Internet)增长的主要应用是电子邮件(email)和万维网(web)，而不是语音通话和电视，这也是电路交换愿景未能实现的另一个原因。

blocks.en: An interesting consequence of these design choices is, users and developers adapted to the realities of packet switching. If you watch a video and the connection is poor, you’re used to the application adapting and the video quality decreasing. (Contrast with broadcast TV, which wouldn’t do this.) This is a lesson in how technology can transform user behavior!
blocks.zh_html: 这些设计选择的一个有趣结果是，用户和开发者已经适应了分组交换(packet switching)的现实。如果你在看视频时网络连接不佳，你已经习惯了应用(application)自适应地降低视频质量。（与不会这样做的广播电视(broadcast TV)形成对比。）这是技术如何改变用户行为的一课！
